experiment.steer: S015 §73 a claim needs uncontended measurement; §77 the metric that counts

headline: THE CAVEAT THREE RECEIPTS CARRIED IS SETTLED AND IT WAS SMALL. A cold read of the staged shard measures 6265.8 MB/s at 99.76% of pages actually coming from disk; cached it is 8318.4 MB/s. The ratio is only 1.33x, so the pipeline's WorkUnits/hour was inflated by cache residency at the level of a few percent, not by a factor.

written_before.third_outcome: below 500 MB/s means 3 MB strided reads are seek-bound

the_prediction_and_both_branches_are_ref.what_happened: F_NOCACHE reads came out FASTER than warm ones (8653 vs 7520 MB/s) and WorkUnits/hour went UP 7.48%. Neither branch allowed that direction.
the_prediction_and_both_branches_are_ref.why: F_NOCACHE asks the kernel not to RETAIN this file's pages. IT DOES NOT EVICT PAGES ALREADY CACHED. So the experiment compared cache against cache, and the ~7% it measured is the cost of retention bookkeeping, not of touching a disk. I designed a contrast that CANNOT PRODUCE THE CONDITION IT NAMES.
the_prediction_and_both_branches_are_ref.how_that_was_caught: vm_stat reports cumulative PAGEINS without sudo. A read that touches the disk must produce pageins; one served from cache produces none. Checking the assumption rather than the man page is what settled it.

the_measurement.instrument: vm_stat Pageins delta across each read, 16384-byte pages, 12288 pages if every byte came from disk

cold_read.how_it_was_obtained: BY ACCIDENT -- the probe's FIRST touch of the file in this process was genuinely cold, which is exactly why it cannot be repeated without evicting

f_nocache_reads.means: F_NOCACHE did NOT produce a cold read; 0.01% pageins is the proof, not an inference

the_substitute_that_does_not_substitute.idea: write a file with F_NOCACHE, then read it back -- its pages should not be resident
the_substitute_that_does_not_substitute.result: EXACTLY 66.67% of pages from disk, on ALL SEVEN samples across two probes (8193, 8193, 8193, 8193, 8193, 8194, 8184 of 12288). A stable ~64 MB window stays resident, which is a third of the file.
the_substitute_that_does_not_substitute.diagnosis_split_two_ways: settling 20 s changes the PAGEIN FRACTION by 0.12% (structural, not write-in-flight) but changes the RATE by +43% (write-in-flight). Both candidate explanations were partly right, on DIFFERENT QUANTITIES, and picking one would have been wrong either way.
the_substitute_that_does_not_substitute.verdict: REFUSED as a cold-read measurement: 46% spread against a 10% gate, and it never reaches the ~100% pagein fraction that would make it cold at all. The 2214-3317 MB/s numbers are NOT quoted as this SSD's cold rate.
the_substitute_that_does_not_substitute.an_instrument_defect_in_my_own_probe: the script's automatic verdict keyed on EXACT EQUALITY of an integer counter, so 8194 vs 8184 -- a 0.12% difference -- was labelled 'settling moves it'. A verdict computed by exact equality of a noisy counter reports noise as a finding.

consequence_for_the_pipeline.means: the 2,151,304 WU/h figure would fall by roughly 7% if every read came from disk. The three receipts that warned it was 'partly page cache, an upper bound' were right to warn and the warning was OVERCAUTIOUS: the cold SSD is 6266 MB/s, ABOVE the 5035.5 MB/s the Tier 1 receipt measured and flagged as cache-inflated.

named_gate.blocked_on: a clean, REPEATABLE cold read needs `sudo purge` or a working set exceeding 96 GiB of RAM
named_gate.why_not_available: sudo is not available to this process, and staging a >96 GiB working set onto Tier 1 costs 437.78 s per 192 MB at the measured Tier 2 rate
named_gate.recorded_as: a NAMED GATE with its exact missing input per §129, alongside the powermetrics/thermal gate and the NVIDIA/P2 gate -- not a parking lot

claim_boundary.n_equals_1_for_the_number_that_matters: the cold read is a SINGLE sample. It is a direct measurement with a 99.76% pagein fraction proving it was cold, but it has no spread and cannot be cited as a characterised disk rate.
claim_boundary.one_file_one_pattern: 192 MB read as 64 sequential 3 MB chunks. Nothing here says anything about random small reads, about writes, or about Tier 2.
claim_boundary.the_lake_fill_was_running: not quiesced for this probe, so the cold sample carries whatever contention the concurrent downloads imposed -- which makes 6266 MB/s a LOWER bound on the quiet-machine cold rate, in the safe direction for the claim

bench.machine: Apple M3 Ultra, 60 GPU cores, 96 GiB (receipts/headless/MACHINE_GENOME.json)
bench.rule: S032 §3 -- if quiescence is unknown the state is UNKNOWN, not quiet
bench.provenance: this receipt was written before quiescence was a benchmark input and recorded none. UNKNOWN is what it measured under, not a claim that the machine was busy
